newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Digitel, BT set to sign telecom pact.
newsitem.headline: Digitel, BT set to sign telecom pact.

text.p: Digital Telecommunications Philippines Inc (Digitel) will sign a correspondentship agreement with British Telecom Plc next week, a Digitel official said on Monday.
William Pamintuan, Digitel senior vice-president, told reporters the agreement will allow Digitel access to the United Kingdom through British Telecom facilities and vice-versa.
As a direct correspondent for Digitel, British Telecom will carry international calls between the Philippines, Europe and Africa, the official said.
At present, Digitel has correspondentship agreements with AT&T Corp, MCI Communications Corp and Teleglobe Inc.
Pamintuan also said Digitel will be able to install 203,000 telephone lines by year-end, slightly higher than its target of 202,000 lines.
By next year, it will be able to put in place an additional 330,000 telephone lines.

Digitel's programme calls for the installation of a total of 1.2 million telephone lines in the area in which it is licensed to operate, which includes the northern island of Luzon except Metro Manila. The company has previously said it will require 40 billion pesos in capital expenditure over a 10-year period ending year 2004.
Pamintuan said Digitel stands firm on its earlier projections of a 707 million peso net income for 1996 despite comments from stock market analysts that the target may be too ambitious.
"We are assuring them that we will meet those targets due to the Christmas season. We should wait. We are not changing our forecast," said Pamintuan.
The company posted profits of 415.4 million pesos for the first nine months of the year.
